body:
Burn-down complete (--status approved). 9 specs, 3 waves, all merged and Completed; ready set empty, no open PRs, integrated main verified green after every wave.

Completed:
  BUG-781   #1586  accepted decisions render terminal, leave the default open lens
  TASK-1170 #1587  edit-preserving --refresh across all agent packs (codex/antigravity parity)
  TASK-1136 #1588  single-branch cluster PR links all members + bumps all Done->Completed
  TASK-1172 #1589  priority-ordered ready set, [burndown] order = priority|queue opt-out
  BUG-782   #1590  aida tail redirects a live drain's fan-out worker to `aida tail drain`
  TASK-1137 #1591  per-member checkpoint hook on the single-branch drain
  BUG-783   #1592  quiet the archived/deferred hidden-count footers by default
  TASK-1173 #1593  aida tail per-event local-time prefixes (pacing signal)
  TASK-1171 #1594  dedicated eval channel so human stdout is never an eval candidate

Substrate change made during the drain: TASK-1136/1137 both extend drain_batch_single_branch, and BUG-782/TASK-1173 both edit tail_cmd.rs. Rather than remember not to co-fan them I tagged each pair serialize:single-branch-drain / serialize:aida-tail, so the gate collapsed them into serialize_held itself and the ordering is now enforced for future drains, not just this one.

Caveats / verifications worth noting:
- Integrated-main verify was a cargo build --workspace compile check (per the skill), not a test run. Ran after each wave; all green. Worth knowing it would not catch a behavioral integration break, only a compile-level one.
- TASK-1136's multi-spec bump rides the EXISTING extract_spec_ids_from_commit multi-id support (its diff is additive only), verified by a round-trip test through the real derive_squash_subject. Not a self-granted capability.
- TASK-1171 changes the aida() wrapper contract. Your CURRENTLY SOURCED wrapper is the old one. The change is capability-negotiated via AIDA_SHELL_WRAPPER, both markers are shell comments, and all four skew combinations are tested, so nothing breaks on upgrade -- but `aida dev status` will now report the wrapper stale until you run `aida dev shell-init --install` and open a new shell. That is the intended upgrade path, not a fault.
- TASK-1171's tests drive real bash only. Filed TASK-1174 for zsh coverage; verified this machine has no zsh and a /bin/bash login shell, so no live exposure.
- TASK-1172's spec premise was imprecise: the ready set was ALREADY id-sorted before the change, so `order = queue` restores id order, not added_at order. Implementation is self-consistent and says so in its comments; the spec/doc wording is what is off. Filed TASK-1175.

Filed during the drain (approved, deliberately NOT queued -- yours to bless, so the drain does not feed itself):
  TASK-1174  zsh coverage for the eval-channel wrapper
  TASK-1175  clarify [burndown] order = queue semantics

Left for manual merge: none.

Held / awaiting sign-off: VIS-1, TASK-1164 (pre-existing), plus TASK-1174, TASK-1175 above.

Parked (unchanged, all pre-existing): TASK-735, TASK-751 (deferred:on-demand); TASK-749 (deferred:future-rbac); TASK-892 (deferred:until-projects-toml-consumed); STORY-687, STORY-688 (deferred:cockpit-phase2); EPIC-44 (epic -- needs decomposition).

Worktrees not pruned: 3 stale locked worktrees from EARLIER drains, all at d9f9eceb8 -- agent-a942df7439695a8aa, agent-ab76dad2f2712ef43, agent-ada058a96e1aba25f. Not mine; left alone rather than pruning another session's state. All 9 of this drain's worktrees + local + remote branches were pruned.
